columns.description: The census tract represents small-area neighborhood units, while the census block is the smallest geographic unit used by the United States Census Bureau for tabulating data. Census tracts and blocks allow for the analysis of demographic and housing information. The field contains the Census Tract ID and Census Block ID as one string with both IDs separated by a period. This string is derived from the 2020 Census.
columns.name: Census Block 2020

body.description: The Seattle Police Department (SPD) replaced its Records Management System (RMS) in May 2019. To preserve data quality and continuity between systems (2008-Present), SPD relied on the National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS). The standardization of crime classifications allows for comparison over time. For more information on definitions and classifications, please visit https://www.fbi.gov/services/cjis/ucr/nibrs. Additional groupings are used to analyze crime in SPD’s Crime Dashboard. Violent and property crime categories align with best practices. For additional inquiries, we encourage the use of the underline data to align with the corresponding query. Disclaimer: Only finalized (UCR approved) reports are released. Those in draft, awaiting approval, or completed after the update, will not appear until the subsequent day(s). Data is updated once every twenty-four hours. Records and classification changes will occur as a report makes its way through the approval and investigative process.
body.name: SPD Crime Data: 2008-Present
